brief: A two-storey storage tower for a workbench with at least two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Bases on level 0 and level 1: piece:0,0,0 and piece:0,0,1 (full), piece:0,1,0 and piece:0,1,1 (half-n).
drawer:0#0,1#cut (lower) and drawer:1#0,1#cut (upper) both face the open front; the upper one is shown open with no collisions.

A small, freestanding unit with end caps and bolted joints, and drawer compartments for small tools (marker and pen placed). The configurator does not check how much weight it can carry or how strong it is.

finish.summary: A two-storey tower: two full hex bases stacked at (0,0), with two half bases stacked in front at (0,1). Each half base holds a drawer that opens toward the user. My first layout put the drawers facing the main column, and the configurator refused to let them open, so I moved the half bases to the open front side. The open faces have end caps and the joints are bolted. The meshes check clear and there are no rule errors. I put a marker and a pen in the open top drawer to show it in use. Bigger props (screw bins, tape, a standing screwdriver) were refused because they didn't fit the drawer compartments.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
